subject: maths
question: Aditya is standing on a light house of 150 m height and watching two boats on either side with angles of depression of 30° and 60°, respectively. Find the distance between the two boats.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects are on opposite sides of a tower of height **h**, the distance between them is directly given by:

Distance = h × (cot θ₁ + cot θ₂)

⇒ Distance = 150 × (cot 30° + cot 60°)

⇒ Distance = 150 × (√3 + 1/√3)

⇒ Distance = 150 × (4 / √3) = 200√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 200√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the lighthouse (AB) = 150 m

Angle of depression of Boat 1 (at C) = 30°

Angle of depression of Boat 2 (at D) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Since alternate interior angles are equal, the angle of elevation of the top of the lighthouse from Boat 1 (C) is 30° and from Boat 2 (D) is 60°.

**Calculations:**

In right-angled triangle ABC:

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 / √3 = 150 ÷ BC

⇒ BC = 150√3 m

In right-angled triangle ABD:

⇒ tan 60° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ √3 = 150 ÷ BD

⇒ BD = 150 ÷ √3

⇒ BD = (150 × √3) ÷ 3 = 50√3 m

Total distance between the two boats (CD) = BC + BD

⇒ CD = 150√3 + 50√3

⇒ CD = 200√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 200√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance Formula for Same Side

If two objects are on the same side of a vertical tower of height **h**, the distance between them is given by **h × |cot θ₁ − cot θ₂|**.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The angle of elevation refers to looking upward from the horizontal line of sight, while the angle of depression refers to looking downward. Geometrically, both angles are equivalent due to alternate interior properties along parallel horizontal lines.

Key Trigonometric Standard Values

Memorise standard tangent ratios for exams: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. Cotangent values are simply their reciprocals.
